query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix, whose overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation behavior across different temperatures remain unclear, what single intervention could improve its wear resistance under sliding conditions spanning different temperatures, friction velocities, and wear depths? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating tested under identical conditions, defines the operating limits of the prediction, cites supporting evidence from the introduction, and proposes a falsification experiment capable of resolving microscopic deformation during wear.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of Ti to the FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating can improve its wear resistance under sliding conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix
generation.intervention: Addition of Ti to the coating
generation.conditions: Sliding conditions spanning different temperatures, friction velocities, and wear depths
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a Ti-rich oxide layer
generation.mechanism: The Ti addition promotes the formation of a protective oxide layer, which reduces wear and improves the coating's resistance to deformation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved wear resistance and reduced deformation of the coating
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 20-500°C, friction velocity range: 0.1-10 m/s, wear depth range: 0.1-10 mm
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of the Ti-rich oxide layer formation and its effect on wear resistance is not fully understood.

falsification_experiment.design: Sliding wear test with varying Ti content and testing conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate and coating deformation increase with Ti addition, the hypothesis is falsified.
